idea:
Add a `--dry-run` / `-n` flag to the `ralph init` command that simulates initialization and prints what would be done without creating any files or directories.

## Summary

The `ralph init` command needs a dry-run mode. When `--dry-run` is passed, the command should print each action it would take (e.g. "would create .ralph/", "would create .ralph/ralph.toml") instead of actually performing them. Default behavior (no flag) must remain unchanged.

## Requirements

- Add `dry_run: bool` field to `InitArgs` in `src/cli/mod.rs`, exposed as `--dry-run` / `-n`
- Pass `dry_run` through to `execute()` in `src/cli/init.rs`
- When `dry_run` is `true`: print each action that would be taken, create no files or directories
- When `dry_run` is `false` (default): behavior is identical to current

## Files to Modify

- `src/cli/mod.rs` — add `dry_run` field to `InitArgs`
- `src/cli/init.rs` — check the flag; print instead of writing when set

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `--dry-run` and `-n` both accepted as CLI flags on `ralph init`
- [ ] Running `ralph init --dry-run` prints lines like "would create .ralph/", "would create .ralph/ralph.toml" for each action
- [ ] No files or directories are created when `--dry-run` is active
- [ ] Running `ralph init` without the flag behaves exactly as before
- [ ] No regressions in existing `init` tests; new test(s) cover dry-run output
